architecture.mechanism: Digital twin-based fault diagnosis using data acquisition, digital modeling, and data analysis to identify hidden motor faults that conventional electrical measurements cannot detect.
architecture.intervention: Construct a digital twin of the 3-phase induction conveyor drive motor using real-time no-load operational data acquisition (current waveforms, vibration spectra, thermal profiles) and compare the physical motor's behavior against the idealized digital model to isolate the specific anomaly causing the 20-minute thermal overload trip despite balanced winding resistance and stable 400V supply.
architecture.expected_effect: The digital twin comparison will reveal the precise non-resistive, non-voltage fault mechanism (such as rotor bar degradation, eccentric air gap, or high-frequency core losses) responsible for the anomalous no-load heating, enabling targeted repair that prevents the thermal overload from tripping.
architecture.falsification_test: If the digital twin model predicts no deviation between the physical motor's acquired no-load data and the idealized model parameters, yet the thermal overload continues to trip at 20 minutes, the digital twin diagnostic mechanism is falsified as insufficient to explain the failure.

challenge.kill_reason: the mechanism-space distinctness adjudication counts 1 materially distinct mechanism(s) (< 2, mechanism_distinctness/2.0.0) — the run generated nothing worth attacking (Art. LXXXIV, R514)
